subject: PineTech: lab readout & next A/B latency tests
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.inference.com>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.inference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: PineTech: lab readout & next A/B latency tests

Hi Carl —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum:

Recap from today's call:
- PineTech wants a focused, measurable A/B that compares Redwood-hosted inference vs the hyperscaler endpoint you currently use (we heard Bedrock/Vertex mentioned).
- Key success criteria: p95 and p99 latency at two sequence lengths (64 tokens / 512 tokens) and steady-state tokens/sec at target concurrency.
- You have a short prompt set (~120 prompts) that represents production mixes (chatty + code + short completions).

Redwood proposed lab scope (attached: pinetech_initial_test_matrix.xlsx):
- Baselines: Hyperscaler baseline + Redwood default model variant + Redwood quantized variant.
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, tail latencies under 60s window, and cost per 1M tokens estimate.
- Test conditions: warm-up 3000 tokens, run each variant for 10 minutes at 5 concurrency levels (1, 4, 8, 16, 32).
- Data: we will run on your sample prompts (attached) and record KV cache hit behavior, cold vs warm-run deltas.

Asks from PineTech:
- Can you confirm a 2-hour lab window this week or early next for us to run the full matrix?
- Please upload the prompt set to the Drive link (we shared) or send back the file.

Next steps I propose:
1) You pick a 2-hour window (we recommend Tue/Wed morning PT).
2) We run one warm-up + 3 full passes, capture p95/p99 and tokens/sec.
3) Post-run: 30-min readout with concrete config recommendations (batch size, quantization level, routing fallbacks).

I've looped in Aditya and Grace for ops & test design. Attachments: initial matrix, sample prompts, and a short PDF baseline we use internally.

If that all looks good, reply with the window you prefer and any constraints (IP/ingress, test IP allowlist).

Thanks,
Lauren

Subject: Re: PineTech: lab readout & next A/B latency tests (test design notes)

Lauren / Grace —

Thanks Carl for the window confirmation. A few technical clarifications and a recommended concrete test plan we should run during the 08:30–10:30 PT slot:

Test design (concise):
- Models: Hyperscaler-approx (same architecture + FP16 where possible), Redwood default FP16, Redwood int8-quant (LLM.int8).
- Sequences: two buckets: short (avg 64 tokens), long (avg 512 tokens). For long we will include a small set of 8 prompts that exercise large KV cache usage.
- Concurrency & batching: run at conc 1 / 4 / 8 / 16 / 32. For each concurrency level we sweep batch sizes 1, 2, 4 to measure batching impact on tokens/sec and tail latency.
- Warm-up: 3 minutes continuous, then capture a 10-minute steady-state window. We will repeat the steady window 3x per variant.

What we will measure: p50/p95/p99 latency per-token and per-request, tokens/sec (aggregate), GPU utilization, memory footprint, and number of requests that hit >1s tail (for reliability).

A/B specifics:
- For the hyperscaler baseline we will match model family and prompt encoding; slight differences in kernel fusion are expected. We'll log model version strings for transparency.
- For cost estimate: we will capture estimated GPU-mins and token counts and provide a back-of-envelope $/1M tokens for each variant (using published price points where applicable).

Operational notes:
- Carl: we will need an allowlist IP range for the runner and SSH access to your telemetry collector for GPU metrics (prometheus endpoint or similar).
- Grace: can you prepare two run scripts (hyperscaler_baseline.sh + redwood_ab.sh) and include a consistent request driver so measurements are comparable? I recommend wrk-style driver with fixed inter-arrival patterns to reproduce burstiness.

I will bring an automated summary notebook that outputs p95/p99 tables and CSVs. That will land in the Drive folder immediately after the run.

-Aditya
Aditya Rao
